To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the protein kinase activity of islet cells increases in the presence of compounds which increase the concentration of cyclic AMP within the cell.
the sulphonylurea, tolbutamide, and the xanthine, 3-isobuty-1-methyl xanthine (IBMX), increase insulin secretion by increasing the intracellular concentration of cAMP in pancreatic islets.
agents which affect cyclic AMP concentrations in the islets affect protein kinase activity and that this effect may be the mechanism by which they affect insulin secretion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mode of action of cyclic AMP in the islet cell.
the mode of action of cyclic AMP and its derivatives in mammalian islet cells.
the mechanism of action of cyclic AMP in the islet cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cyclic AMP-dependent protein kinases are not involved in the regulation of insulin secretion by glucose.
cyclic AMP is a second messenger in the regulation of insulin release.
protein kinase is a key component in the mode of action of cyclic AMP on insulin secretion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cyclic AMP system plays an important role in the regulation of insulin secretion.
the protein kinase activity of the pancreatic islet cells was dependent on the concentration of cyclic AMP in the cells.
cyclic AMP-dependent protein phosphorylation is a key step in the mechanism of insulin secretion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
protein kinase A (PKA), which is the enzyme responsible for phosphorylating and activating the KATP channels in beta cells, is also responsible for activating insulin secretion in beta cells.
the effects of sulfonylurea drugs on insulin secretion are mediated by the ATP-sensitive K+ channel and that the ATP-sensitive K channel is the primary target of sulfonyluraes in the beta-cell.
